712927.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tréyes, from Proto-Indo-European *tréyes. Cognates include Sanskrit त्रि (tri), Latin trēs, Old Armenian երեք (erekʻ) and Old English þrēo (English three).

712903.t: Seemingly an inherited term, though the broad semantic range of the word makes ascertaining further origin and cognates difficult: * If from Proto-Indo-European *top-o-s: ** From Proto-Indo-European *tep- (“to hit, stick, smear”), and cognate with…

712928.t: From Proto-Hellenic *trémō, from Proto-Indo-European *trem- (“to tremble”), extended form of Proto-Indo-European *ter-. The extended form Proto-Indo-European *tres- also yielded τρέω (tréō, “to dread, to terrify”).

712934.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tridḱómt (“thirty”). Cognates include Latin trīgintā, Sanskrit त्रिंशत् (triṃśát) and Old Armenian երեսուն (eresun).

712917.t: From τράγω (trágō, “to gnaw, nibble”) + -ος (-os, “nominal suffix”), literally “gnawer, eater (of sweets)”.

712919.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tr̥-ped-ih₂- (“having three feet”), from *tr̥- (“three”, combining form) + *pṓds (“foot”) + *-ih₂ (feminine nominal suffix).

712984.t: From τρέφω (tréphō, “to maintain, support”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

712940.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tr-ey-gʷ-, from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to rub”). Cognate with Latin tero.

712931.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ- (“to run, drag”), suppleted in the future and aorist tenses with *drem- (“to run”).

712994.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰrogʰós (possibly an -ός (-ós) nominal), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ- (“to run, drag, pull”), whence τρέχω (trékhō, “to run”).

712925.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰrākʰús (whence Mycenaean Greek 𐀲𐀨𐀐𐀹(𐀊) (ta-ra-ke-wi(ja))), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰréh₂gʰ-us ~ *dʰr̥h₂gʰ-éws (“rough”), from *dʰreh₂gʰ- (“to irritate”). Compare θράσσω (thrā́ssō).

712930.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tʰrépʰō with deaspiration of the /tʰ/ to /t/ by Grassmann's law everywhere except in forms where the /pʰ/ has been deaspirated to /p/ by a following consonant (future, first aorist, perfect middle).

712929.t: From Proto-Indo-European *trep- (“to turn”); cognate with Latin trepit (“turns”, verb), Sanskrit त्रपते (trápate, “feels ashamed, becomes timid or perplexed”), and Hittite 𒋼𒊑𒅁𒍣 (te-ri-ip-zi /⁠teripzi⁠/, “to plough”).

712968.t: From Proto-Indo-European *tr̥tyós ~ *tritós, thus an inherited ordinal to τρεῖς (treîs, “three”), as if formed with Proto-Indo-European *-tós.

712976.t: From τροπαῖος (tropaîos, “of defeat”), from τροπή (tropḗ, “rout, turning of an enemy”).

712932.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tréhō, from Proto-Indo-European *tréseti. Cognates include Latin terreō, Old Irish tarrach, and Sanskrit त्रसति (trasati).

712939.t: From τρίβω (tríbō, “rub, grind”). Compare typologically Russian тропа́ (tropá) (akin to трепа́ть (trepátʹ).

712920.t: From τιτρώσκω (titrṓskō, “to wound”) + -μα (-mă, suffix forming neuter nouns).

712908.t: Proto-Hellenic *tókʷe, from Proto-Indo-European *to- + *-kʷe. Compare ὅτε (hóte), πότε (póte).

712975.t: From τρέμω (trémō) + -ος (-os), from Proto-Indo-European *trem- (“to tremble”). Cognate with Tocharian B tremi (“anger”).

712906.t: From Proto-Hellenic *tótsos, earlier *tótyos, from Proto-Indo-European *tóti, adverb from *só. Cognate with Sanskrit तति (táti), Latin tot.

712953.t: From Proto-Hellenic *trís, from Proto-Indo-European *trís; related to τρεῖς (treîs, “three”). Cognates include Sanskrit त्रिस् (trís) and Latin ter.

712995.t: No clear etymology. Furnée connects the word with τρίβανον (tríbanon, “oil flask”), considering it to be of Pre-Greek origin.

712987.t: From τροχάνη (trokhánē, “wheel, axle, gear”) + -τήρ (-tḗr), from τροχάζω (trokházō, “to run quickly”).

712974.t: By surface analysis, τρόμος (trómos) + -έω (-éō). However, it may also derive from Proto-Hellenic *troméyō, from Proto-Indo-European *troméyeti, a causative from *trem- (“to tremble”) + *-éyeti.

712977.t: Possibly inherited from Proto-Hellenic *tropéyō, from Proto-Indo-European *trop-éye-ti, from *trep-.
